text: 74-year-old male. The patient presents with sudden onset of abdominal pain around the umbilicus 16 hours ago, with recent history of hospitalization for an acute myocardial infarction a week ago. Reports several episodes of bloody loose bowel movements. Denies vomiting.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent heart attack and the sudden onset of bloody stools, is the pain constant or does it come and go, and have you noticed any fever or chills? Also, does the pain feel worse after eating, and are you experiencing any dizziness or lightheadedness?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe abdominal pain. I also have Bloody loose bowel movements, No vomiting, Sudden onset.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of severe umbilical pain, bloody stools, and your recent heart attack is highly concerning for a lack of blood flow to your intestines. I need to check for signs of tissue death and confirm the diagnosis immediately. REQUEST TEST: CT_Angiography_Abdomen_Pelvis.

text: RESULTS: CT_Angiography_Abdomen: Findings show evidence suggestive of reduced blood flow to the mesenteric arteries. Vital signs show a heart rate of 95 bpm and blood pressure of 95/65 mm Hg. Note: Respiratory rate, WBC, Hemoglobin, Platelets, Creatinine, BUN, and Glucose results were not provided in the available data.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the CT findings of reduced mesenteric blood flow and your recent heart attack, I am highly suspecting acute mesenteric ischemia. To confirm the extent of tissue damage and guide treatment, I need to see the actual scans. REQUEST IMAGES.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Known diabetes mellitus for 35 years and hypertension for 20 years. History of acute myocardial infarction. Social history: Smokes 15–20 cigarettes per day for the past 40 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Your history of heavy smoking, long-standing diabetes, and recent heart attack strongly supports the diagnosis of acute mesenteric ischemia caused by poor blood flow to your intestines. Given the CT evidence of reduced flow and your symptoms, I have enough information to proceed. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Mesenteric Ischemia.
